places.name: Ushguli Village (UNESCO Site)
places.ai_summary: A picturesque village in the Caucasus Mountains, known for its medieval towers and stunning alpine scenery.

opening_hours.notes: Accessible year-round, but best visited in summer.

places.place_tip: Wear comfortable shoes for exploring the village and its surroundings.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited during daylight hours for safety.

places.place_tip: Bring water and snacks for the hike to the glacier.

places.name: Svaneti Museum of History and Ethnography
places.ai_summary: A museum showcasing the rich history, culture, and traditions of the Svaneti region, including ancient artifacts and manuscripts.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on public holidays.

places.place_tip: Don’t miss the ancient icons and manuscripts on display.

places.ai_summary: A popular ski resort near Mestia, offering a range of winter sports and activities in the stunning Caucasus Mountains.

opening_hours.notes: Open during the winter season, typically from December to April.

places.place_tip: Book ski passes and equipment rentals in advance during peak season.

places.name: Koruldi Lakes
places.ai_summary: A stunning glacial lake located a short hike from Mestia, known for its crystal-clear waters and picturesque surroundings.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the summer months when the trail is clear of snow.

places.place_tip: Take the trail early to avoid afternoon clouds obscuring the view.

places.name: Svan Towers (Defensive Architecture)
places.ai_summary: Medieval stone towers that are a symbol of Svaneti, offering insight into the region's historical defense structures.

opening_hours.notes: Best viewed from the outside; some towers may be closed to the public.

places.place_tip: Respect the privacy of the residents when visiting tower houses.

places.place_tip: Bring a flashlight to see the frescoes clearly.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the summer months; access may be restricted in winter.
